label: Days Since El Mencho Killed
deltaNote: Day 210. 'EL SEÑOR DE LA T' ARRESTED — BAJÍO MICHOACÁN (Sep 17): Security Secretary García Harfuch announced the arrest of Manuel Alejandro Rendón Aguilar, alias 'El Señor de la T,' a CJNG regional coordinator across Angamacutiro, Penjamillo, Panindícuaro, José Sixto Verduzco and Puruándiro in Michoacán's Bajío region, with a close operational relationship to fellow regional commander 'Tío Lako.' He faced warrants for homicide and forced disappearance tied to a 2025 síndico killing and a former mayor's disappearance. Day 207. CJNG MEMBERSHIP ESTIMATE (Sep 15): Infobae cited U.S. NCTC/DEA estimates putting CJNG membership at 15,000-20,000 — larger than the armed forces of Paraguay, Sweden, Denmark or Ireland — under Juan Carlos Valencia González ('El 03'), with revenue from extortion, fuel theft, kidnapping, illegal logging/mining, human trafficking and timeshare fraud beyond narcotics. 'EL BRILLOSO' LINKED TO TRIAL (Sep 15): A control judge formally linked Alexis Jesús Medina García, 'El Brilloso,' to trial for qualified homicide in the Carlos Manzo assassination, ordering preventive detention at the Charo, Michoacán high-security prison and giving prosecutors two months for further investigation. Day 205. TIJUANA ARREST — 'EL NETO' (Sep 13): Baja California state police (FESC) captured José Ernesto 'N,' alias 'El Neto,' an alleged CJNG collaborator, in the Pedregal de Santa Julia neighborhood of Tijuana; he is linked to the killing of a state security officer and suspected arms trafficking, and was transferred to the FGR. POLICE-KILLINGS REPORT — JALISCO LEADS (Sep 10-11): Civil organization Causa en Común reported 212 Mexican security-force members killed nationally in 2026 (85 municipal police, 66 state police, 44 National Guard, 11 Army, 4 federal police, 2 Navy); Jalisco led all states with 36 cases, followed by Michoacán (29) and Sinaloa (25). Day 204. ARMY-CJNG CLASH — JILOTLÁN DE LOS DOLORES (Sep 13): Army Special Forces, National Guard and the FGR raided two suspected CJNG narco-camps in Jilotlán de los Dolores, southern Jalisco, and came under gunfire; 4 suspected gunmen and 1 soldier were killed, a second soldier wounded, and a .50-cal Barrett rifle, other long guns, ~138 IEDs and 6 vehicles seized. A related raid in Santa María del Oro dismantled a clandestine methamphetamine lab. Day 202. CJNG CLANDESTINE 'HOSPITAL' FOUND — TECALITLÁN (Sep 10-11): Jalisco authorities, the National Guard and SEDENA raided a property in Tecalitlán used by CJNG as a recovery clinic for wounded members, rescuing 8 held men and detaining 6 suspects on human-trafficking and forced-disappearance charges; Security Secretary García Harfuch confirmed the federal investigation Sep 11. LOS VALLARTA ARREST — LA PAZ, EDOMEX (Sep 10): State of Mexico prosecutors arrested an alleged financial operator of 'Los Vallarta,' a CJNG-linked cell, over an August 1 bar killing. 'EL BRILLOSO' ARRESTED — CARLOS MANZO CASE (Sep 9): Alexis Jesús Medina García, an alleged CJNG-linked regional operator in Uruapan, Michoacán, was arrested in Zapopan, Jalisco — the 32nd detainee in the Carlos Manzo assassination case. Day 200. CJNG CAR-BOMB STRATEGY ANALYSIS (Sep 9): Infobae cited security researcher Víctor Sánchez Valdés framing CJNG's car-bomb campaign as clustering on its 'criminal frontiers' — Guanajuato, Michoacán, and Zacatecas — where the cartel is contesting territory against rivals, ahead of 2027 gubernatorial elections in those states. LOS MEZCALES FINANCIAL HIT (Sep 8): Colima SSPC, SEMAR/Unopes and the FGE captured Abel 'N,' an alleged second-level Los Mezcales logistics/financial operator wanted in Jalisco for aggravated homicide, and his accountant Marcos 'N,' in the Las Parotas neighborhood of Colima municipality; two long guns seized. INTENSIFICATION ANALYSIS (Sep 5): Fortune reported Zacatecas has logged 23 explosive attacks in 2026 (6 car/motorcycle bombs); Brookings' Vanda Felbab-Brown said cartels are showing 'steady intensification of violence' via bomb-laden drones and IEDs. Day 197. COLIMA ARREST — 'EL BALDO' (Sep 6): Colima state security forces, SEMAR/Unopes, and FGR captured Oswaldo Rafael 'N,' alias 'El Baldo,' in Cuauhtémoc municipality — an alleged regional CJNG operator tied to extortion of ranchers and linked to a Sep 2025 prosecutor's-office shooting, an Oct 2025 ex-mayor killing, and the Mar 2026 killing of a cattle-association leader. Day 196. EL 03 EXTRADITION ORDER CONFIRMED (Sep 4): Security Secretary García Harfuch confirmed a U.S. extradition order and dual Mexican-U.S. nationality for Juan Carlos Valencia González ('El 03'), El Mencho's stepson and U.S.-identified CJNG successor — born in Santa Ana, California; previously led the 'Elite Group' armed wing. OJOCALIENTE INVESTIGATION WIDENS (Sep 4): Harfuch disclosed ~200kg of explosives were used in the Aug 30 car bomb and confirmed two more detainees (Hipólito 'N,' Miguel 'N'), tied to an Aguascalientes-Zacatecas surveillance cell; a CJNG–Cártel del Pacífico turf dispute is now a lead investigative theory alongside the earlier retaliation motive. MANZANILLO ARREST (Sep 1): Colima SSPC/SEMAR detained two suspected CJNG/Los Mezcales members, seizing a 40mm grenade launcher. CHALCO ARREST (Sep 3): Mexico State forces detained two suspects with a large drug cache in Chalco, Edomex, on an unconfirmed suspected CJNG-cell link. Day 192. OJOCALIENTE CAR BOMB TOLL REVISED, FIRST ARREST, MILITARY DEPLOYED (Aug 30–Sep 2): Updated official figures put the Aug 30 Ojocaliente, Zacatecas car bomb (attributed to CJNG) at 11 wounded and ~40 homes affected. Zacatecas authorities detained the first suspect, Juan Pedro 'N,' in Cuauhtémoc municipality Sep 1, carrying a homemade explosive, a grenade, and spike strips. SEDENA activated Plan DN-III-E and deployed a 'Genaro Codina' military task force to Ojocaliente Sep 2. The bombing was the third of a three-attack wave (El Chique dam ambush Aug 27, Villa García motorcycle bomb Aug 29) and CJNG's first documented vehicle-borne device of the post-Mencho campaign. R-2 NAMED LOS RS SUCCESSOR, CHARGED (Aug 27): A Washington, D.C. federal grand jury indicted 'El R-1' (arrested Jul 30) and his brother Rafael Álvarez Ayala ('El R-2'), identified by Mexican authorities as R-1's successor atop the CJNG-affiliated 'Los Rs' cell in Michoacán; R-2 remains at large. CJNG DRONE UNIT SPANS 5 STATES (Aug 26): InSight Crime detailed CJNG's 'Operadores Droneros' unit adapting commercial drones for IED drops, chemical payloads, and a helicopter attack across Michoacán, Guanajuato, Chihuahua, Jalisco, and Baja California. 20 MORE CJNG DETAINED, EXOTIC ANIMALS SEIZED (Aug 24): García Harfuch announced 20 alleged CJNG members detained in Aug 21-23 raids across 36 properties in Hidalgo, Jalisco, and Michoacán; combined with the Aug 19 Tío Lako-cell raid, 32 total CJNG members detained in under a week. SUCCESSION BINARY HOLDS: El 03 (confirmed leader, $25M) vs. El Sapo (military wing/Puerto Vallarta plaza boss, $15M) — both remain at large.
